newsitem.title: SPAIN: Germany's Kohl has special place at NATO table.
newsitem.headline: Germany's Kohl has special place at NATO table.

text.p: German Chancellor Helmut Kohl is one NATO leader who carries more weight than others at this week's Madrid summit -- and he's getting an extra large chair because of it.
The organisers of the historic Madrid summit, where Kohl's voice could be crucial in critical arguments about NATO expansion, have done all they can to make the burly German leader comfortable.

Kohl, whose weight fluctuates between 115 and 120 kg (250 and 262 lbs), will enjoy a leather chair a few centimetres wider than the others that President Bill Clinton and leaders from 14 other nations at the summit will be using.

"It looks the same as the other 15 chairs, but it is a little bit wider," said one NATO official of the chair, custom-made for the 1.93 metre (six feet four inch) chancellor. "If you didn't know it was wider, you probably couldn't tell."

Germans sometimes call their avuncular chancellor "The Fat Man" -- without offence. Kohl, 67, often jokes about his weight though he spends several weeks on holiday fasting in the Austrian Alps each year.
Clinton even joked with Kohl about his girth at a NATO summit in Brussels in 1994, telling the chancellor he had seen Japanese sumo wrestlers on television and they had reminded him of Kohl.
